Hi, try this:

g<-ggplot(dat,aes(as.Date(Measurement_Date,"%m/%d/%Y"),log10(ECe_mean),group=Field_Number,
colour=Region),ylim=c(0,2),lwd=2,col=Region)
g+geom_line(alpha=1/2.5,size=2)+ylim(0,2)+xlim(as.Date("6/1/1999","%m/%d/%Y"),as.Date("9/1/2005","%m/%d/%Y"))
+ scale_colour_manual(values=c("red","blue"))

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: geom_line and colour argument
parts:
Hi, in your case, probably it is the easiest way to draw US and DS
layers separately:

g<-ggplot(dat,aes(as.Date(Measurement_Date,"%m/%d/%Y"),log10(ECe_mean),group=Field_Number),ylim=c(0,2),lwd=2)
+
geom_line(data=subset(dat, Region=="US"), mapping=aes(colour="US"),
alpha=1,size=2) +
geom_line(data=subset(dat, Region=="DS"),
mapping=aes(colour="DS"),alpha=1,size=2) +

ylim(0,2)+xlim(as.Date("6/1/1999","%m/%d/%Y"),as.Date("9/1/2005","%m/%d/%Y"))
+

scale_colour_manual(name="Region", values=c("red","blue"))

The layers are drawn in that order.
--
